subject: MATH
question: The ratio of ages of two students is 5 ∶ 4. The difference between their ages is 8 years. What is the age of the younger student?
solution:
**Given:**

Age ratio = 5 ∶ 4

Age difference = 8 years

Find younger student's age

**Concept: **

Ratio of two quantities of the same kind and in the same units is a fraction that shows how many times the one quantity is of the other.

**Solution:**

Difference in ratio = 5 - 4 = 1

Age corresponding to 1 part in ratio = Age difference = 8 years

Younger student's age = 4 parts in ratio × Age corresponding to 1 part in ratio = 4 × 8 = 32 years

**Hence, the age of the younger student is 32 years (Option 2).**

question: In a joint family of 16 persons, the eldest and the youngest members have an age difference of 82 years. If these two are left out of the counting, then the average age of the remaining 14 persons is 28. The average age of the entire family being 30, what is the age of the eldest person?
solution:
**Given:**

The difference of an age of the eldest and youngest members = 82 years

The average age of remaining 14 persons = 28

The average age of the entire family = 30

**Formula used:**

Average = sum of observations/Number of observations

**Calculation:**

Let the age of eldest and youngest be x and y respectively

The difference of an age of the eldest and youngest members = 82 years

⇒ (x – y) = 82 ....(1)

Now,

The average age of remaining 14 persons = (14 × 28) = 392

The average age of the entire family = (16 × 30) = 480

The age of the eldest and youngest family = (480 – 392) = 88

So,

(x + y) = 88 ....(2)

Now,

Adding equation (1) and (2), we get 

⇒ (x – y) = 82 + (x + y) = 88

⇒ 2x = (88 + 82)

⇒ 2x = 170

⇒ x = 85 years

**∴ The age of the eldest person is 85 years**

question: Three years ago, the average age of A, B and C was 29 years. If the average age of B and C, 5 years ago, was 23 years, then what is the present age (in years) of A?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present average of A, B, and C = 29 + 3 = 32 years.

Present sum of ages of A, B, and C = 32 × 3 = 96 years.

Present average of B and C = 23 + 5 = 28 years.

Present sum of ages of B and C = 28 × 2 = 56 years.

Present age of A = 96 − 56 = 40 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average age of A, B, and C, 3 years ago = 29 years

Average age of B and C, 5 years ago = 23 years

**Formula Used:**

Sum of ages = Average age × Number of persons

 Present Age Sum Distribution
 
 
 Sum of Present Ages of A, B, C = 96
 
 
• 
 

 
 
 Sum of B, C = 56
 
 
 Age of A = 40
 
 +

 A = 96 − 56 = 40 years

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of ages of A, B, and C (3 years ago) = 29 × 3 = 87 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of A, B, and C = 87 + (3 persons × 3 years) = 87 + 9 = 96 years

⇒ Sum of ages of B and C (5 years ago) = 23 × 2 = 46 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of B and C = 46 + (2 persons × 5 years) = 46 + 10 = 56 years

⇒ Present age of A = (Present sum of A, B, and C) − (Present sum of B and C)

⇒ Present age of A = 96 − 56 = 40 years

**∴ The correct answer is 40 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Change in Average

If every individual value in a group increases by 'k' years (like aging), then the average of the group also increases by exactly 'k' years.

Combined Group Value

The sum of elements in a larger group minus the sum of elements in its subset will always yield the sum of the remaining uncounted elements.

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of any two persons remains constant throughout their lifetime, regardless of past or future progression.

question: Four years ago, the average age of a group of five members was 38 years. One more man joins the group and the present average age of the group members becomes 44 years. What is the present age (in years) of the new member?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Present average age of the 5 members = 38 + 4 = 42 years.

New average age of the 6 members = 44 years.

Age of new member = New Average + Old Members × Increase in Average

Age of new member = 44 + 5 × (44 − 42)

Age of new member = 44 + 10 = 54 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 54 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Average age of 5 members 4 years ago = 38 years

⇒ Present average age of 6 members (with new member) = 44 years

 Present Ages Representation
 
 5 Members' Present Age = 210
 
 
 5 Members' Present Age = 210
 New: 54
 

 Total 6 Members' Present Age = 264

**Calculations:**

⇒ Present average age of the initial 5 members = 38 + 4 = 42 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of these 5 members = 5 × 42 = 210 years

⇒ Present sum of ages of all 6 members = 6 × 44 = 264 years

⇒ Present age of the new member = 264 − 210 = 54 years

**∴ The correct answer is 54 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Concept of Age Progression

If the average age of a group is A years, then after t years, the average age of the same group becomes A + t years, provided no members are added or removed.

Inclusion of a New Member

Age of new member = New Average + Old Number of Members × Change in Average.

Weighted Average

When two groups with n₁ and n₂ members and averages A₁ and A₂ are mixed, the combined average is (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

question: Five years from now, the ratio of the ages of A, B and C will be 3 ∶ 5 ∶ 2. The sum of the squares of their present ages is 525. What is the present age of B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let's use the option verification method to find B's present age.

If B's present age = 20 years, his age after 5 years = 25 years.

Since the future ratio A : B : C = 3 : 5 : 2, the common multiplier is 25 ÷ 5 = 5.

Present ages of A and C will be (15 − 5) = 10 years and (10 − 5) = 5 years respectively.

Sum of squares = 10² + 20² + 5² = 100 + 400 + 25 = 525 (Matches the given sum perfectly).

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the ages of A, B, and C after 5 years = 3 : 5 : 2

Sum of the squares of their present ages = 525

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ab4f153fc297e5bd286bc787fb04095be5bb8d4cf5d7ef99c78518718f84557.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the ages of A, B, and C after 5 years be 3x, 5x, and 2x respectively.

⇒ Present age of A = (3x − 5)

⇒ Present age of B = (5x − 5)

⇒ Present age of C = (2x − 5)

According to the given condition, the sum of their present age squares is 525:

⇒ (3x − 5)² + (5x − 5)² + (2x − 5)² = 525

⇒ (9x² − 30x + 25) + (25x² − 50x + 25) + (4x² − 20x + 25) = 525

⇒ 38x² − 100x + 75 = 525

⇒ 38x² − 100x − 450 = 0

Dividing the entire equation by 2:

⇒ 19x² − 50x − 225 = 0

⇒ 19x² − 95x + 45x − 225 = 0

⇒ 19x(x − 5) + 45(x − 5) = 0

⇒ (19x + 45)(x − 5) = 0

Since age cannot be a negative value, x = 5.

⇒ Present age of B = 5x − 5

⇒ Present age of B = 5 × 5 − 5 = 20 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Multiplier

When a ratio like a : b : c is given, the actual quantities can be calculated by assuming a common variable (ax, bx, cx).

Quadratic Roots Formula

The roots of ax² + bx + c = 0 can also be calculated using the quadratic formula: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.

Ages Rule

If the present age is x, then the age n years ago was (x − n) and the age n years from now will be (x + n).
</p

question: After 4 years, Ramesh's age will be 50% more than what his age was 16 years ago. What is his present age?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Age (after 4 years) to Age (16 years ago) = 150% : 100% = 3 : 2.

Total time gap between the two periods = 4 + 16 = 20 years.

Difference in ratio parts = 3 − 2 = 1 part.

1 part = 20 years ⇒ Age 16 years ago (2 parts) = 20 × 2 = 40 years.

Present age = 40 + 16 = 56 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 56 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

After 4 years, Ramesh's age will be 50% more than what his age was 16 years ago.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f529f6312b6cd3a676c516157317e4d29ce5fbf15a9fb3fd82d98607e0208b73.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the present age of Ramesh be x years.

⇒ Ramesh's age 16 years ago = (x − 16) years

⇒ Ramesh's age after 4 years = (x + 4) years

⇒ Age after 4 years = Age 16 years ago + 50% of Age 16 years ago

⇒ x + 4 = 1.5 × (x − 16)

⇒ x + 4 = 1.5x − 24

⇒ 1.5x − x = 24 + 4

⇒ 0.5x = 28

⇒ x = 28 ÷ 0.5

⇒ x = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Method for Ages

When comparing ages across different times, the time gap corresponds to the change in ratio parts. Equating the ratio difference to the actual years gap provides the value of 1 ratio part directly.

Handling Percentages in Equations

If a value is P% more than a base value, it is equivalent to (100 + P)% of the base value. Here, 50% more implies 150% of the past age, giving a ratio of 150:100 or 3:2.

Linear Time Gaps

If the present age is x, then the age n years ago is (x − n), and the age m years hence is (x + m). The total time difference between these two points is always (n + m) years.
</p

question: 4 years ago, the age of Garvit was three times that of Yuvansh, but one year ago the age of Garvit was two times that of Yuvansh. What is the difference between the ages of Garvit and Yuvansh?
solution:
**Given:**

4 years ago, the age of Garvit was three times that of Yuvansh, but one year ago the age of Garvit was two times that of Yuvansh.

**Method used:**

Elimination method of linear equation in two variable

**Calculation:**

Let the present age of Garvit be x years and the present age of Yuvansh be y years.

Then, 4 years ago, x - 4 = 3 × (y - 4)...(1)

And one year ago, x - 1 = 2 × (y - 1) ...(2)

Subtracting (2) from (1),

- 3 = y - 10

y = 7 

Substituting y = 7 in (1),

x = 3 × (7 - 4) + 4 = 13 

**∴ The difference between the ages of Garvit and Yuvansh is 13 - 7 = 6 years.**

question: The ratio of the present ages of Ram and Shyam is 3 : 4, and 4 years ago the ratio was 2 : 3. What will be the ratio of the ages of Ram and Shyam 4 years from now?
solution:
**Given:**

Current age ratio of Ram and Shyam = 3 : 4.

Age ratio 4 years ago = 2 : 3.

**Formula Used:**

The ratio of ages can be calculated using the relationship:

Current age = Age a few years ago + Number of years passed.

**Calculation:**

Let Ram's current age be 3x and Shyam's current age be 4x.

Four years ago, ages were:

Ram's age = 3x - 4 and Shyam's age = 4x - 4.

The given ratio 4 years ago was 2 : 3, hence:

(3x - 4) / (4x - 4) = 2 / 3.

9x - 12 = 8x - 8.

9x - 8x = -8 + 12.

x = 4.

Ram's age in 4 years = 12 + 4 = 16 years.

Shyam's age in 4 years = 16 + 4 = 20 years.

The ratio of their ages 4 years from now:

16 : 20 = 4 : 5.

**Therefore, the ratio of the ages of Ram and Shyam 4 years from now will be 4 : 5.**

question: The ratio of the present ages of a mother and a son is 4 : 1 Fourteen years from now, the ratio of their ages will be 2 : 1. The present age (in years) of the mother is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the **ratio difference** by making the **age gap** constant between the mother and son.

Present Ratio = 4 : 1 (Gap = 3 units) | Future Ratio (after 14 years) = 2 : 1 (Gap = 1 unit).

Multiply the future ratio by 3 to equalize gaps: Future Ratio = 6 : 3.

Increase in units for Mother = 6 − 4 = 2 units → 2 units = 14 years → 1 unit = 7 years.

Present age of **Mother** = 4 units × 7 = 28 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present age ratio (Mother : Son) = **4 : 1**

Ratio after 14 years = **2 : 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd113e833a9597809bd493e87888c098fd74b956f1f79288f210d6ef5a9e3295.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the present age of the **Mother** be 4x and the **Son** be x.

⇒ According to the question, after 14 years:

⇒ (4x + 14) / (x + 14) = 2 / 1

⇒ 4x + 14 = 2 × (x + 14)

⇒ 4x + 14 = 2x + 28

⇒ 4x − 2x = 28 − 14

⇒ 2x = 14

⇒ x = 7

⇒ Present age of Mother = 4x = 4 × 7 = 28 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two persons **always remains constant**, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Balancing Method

To solve age problems quickly, multiply the ratios by the **difference of the other ratio** to ensure the unit change is consistent with the time elapsed.

Cross-Product Method

For a ratio a:b becoming c:d after x years, use the formula: 1 unit = [x × (c − d)] / [(a × d) − (b × c)].</p

question: ((3.5)³ - (0.5)³ - 8.75)/((3.5)² - (0.5)² - 3.5) = ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Evaluate the numerator: 3.5³ − 0.5³ − 8.75 = 42.875 − 0.125 − 8.75 = 34

Evaluate the denominator: 3.5² − 0.5² − 3.5 = 12.25 − 0.25 − 3.5 = 8.5

Required Value = 34 ÷ 8.5 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: [(3.5)³ − (0.5)³ − 8.75] ÷ [(3.5)² − (0.5)² − 3.5]

Step 1: Calculate the values of squares and cubes.

⇒ 3.5² = 12.25 and 0.5² = 0.25

⇒ 3.5³ = 42.875 and 0.5³ = 0.125

Step 2: Substitute values into the expression.

⇒ Numerator = 42.875 − 0.125 − 8.75 = 42.75 − 8.75 = 34

⇒ Denominator = 12.25 − 0.25 − 3.5 = 12 − 3.5 = 8.5

Step 3: Perform final division.

⇒ Value = 34 ÷ 8.5

⇒ Value = 340 ÷ 85 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Algebraic Identities

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) and a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b).

Decimal Multiplication

When multiplying decimals, multiply as whole numbers and place the decimal point such that the number of decimal places equals the sum of places in the factors.

question: If a = 3 + sqrt{2}, b = 3 - sqrt{2} , then what is the value of a² + b² ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For conjugates a = x + √y and b = x − √y, the sum of squares is given by 2(x² + y).

Here x = 3 and √y = √2 ⇒ y = 2.

Calculation: 2 × (3² + 2) = 2 × (9 + 2) = 2 × 11 = 22.

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: a = 3 + √2 and b = 3 − √2

Formula: (x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy and (x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy

⇒ a² = (3 + √2)² = 3² + (√2)² + 2 × 3 × √2 ⇒ a² = 9 + 2 + 6√2 = 11 + 6√2 ⇒ b² = (3 − √2)² = 3² + (√2)² − 2 × 3 × √2 ⇒ b² = 9 + 2 − 6√2 = 11 − 6√2 ⇒ a² + b² = (11 + 6√2) + (11 − 6√2) ⇒ a² + b² = 22

**∴ The correct answer is 22.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Squares Identity

For any two numbers, (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). This is useful for solving symmetric expressions.

Rationalization Conjugates

The product of conjugates (x + √y)(x − √y) = x² − y is always a rational number.

Algebraic Expansion

Square of a binomial: (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.

question: On a tree, there are some parrots and some pigeons in the ratio of 7 ∶ 9, respectively. After an hour, 8 parrots fly away, and 6 pigeons and 10 sparrows come and sit on the tree. The ratio of the parrots and the pigeons on the tree now is 1 ∶ 4. What is the ratio of the parrots and the sparrows that are now on the tree?

⇒ 28x – 32 = 9x + 6

⇒ 28x – 9x = 6 + 32 = 38

⇒ x = (38)/(19) = 2

Number of parrots on tree now = 7 × 2 – 8 = 14 – 8 = 6

Number of sparrows on tree = 10

Ratio of number of parrots to number of sparrows

= (6)/(10) = 3 : 5

**Hence, the ratio of number of parrots to the number of sparrows on tree is 3 : 5.**

question: The sum of the two numbers is the same as nine times their difference. The ratio of the numbers is:
solution:
**Given:**

The sum of the two numbers is the same as nine times their difference.

**Formula Used:**

Let the two numbers be x and y.

Sum of the numbers = x + y

Difference of the numbers = |x - y|

Sum = 9 × Difference

**Calculation:**

⇒ x + y = 9(x - y)

Let's assume x > y, so the difference x - y is positive.

⇒ x + y = 9x - 9y

Bringing like terms to one side,

⇒ 9y + y = 9x - x

⇒ 10y = 8x

Dividing both sides by 8y,

⇒ x/y = 10/8

⇒ x/y = 5/4

Therefore, the ratio of the numbers is 5 : 4.

**The ratio of the numbers is 5 : 4.**

question: Due to a fault in the voting machine, the invalid votes are counted in votes of the candidate B, who gets 5 times the invalid votes. A gets the votes 8 times the invalid votes and wins the election by 28. What is the total number of votes polled?
solution:
**Given:**

Invalid votes are counted in votes of candidate B.

Candidate B gets 5 times the invalid votes.

Candidate A gets 8 times the invalid votes.

Candidate A wins by 28 votes.

Calculation:

Invalid votes = x

Votes for candidate A = 8x

Votes for candidate B = 5x

Votes for candidate B because of faulty machine = 5x + x = 6x

We are given that A wins by 28 votes, so:

Votes for A - Votes for B = 28

8x - 6x = 28

2x = 28

x = 14

Total votes = Votes for A + Votes for B + Invalid votes

Total votes = 8x + 5x + x

Total votes = 14 × 14 = 196

**The total number of votes polled is 196.**

So, we can write:

25 * (81/4) = x * x

Simplifying this equation, we get:

25 * 81 / 4 = x²

2025 / 4 = x²

Taking the square root of both sides, we get:

x = ±√(2025 / 4)

question: Two mixers and one TV cost ₹7,000, while two TVs and one mixer cost ₹9,800. The value of one TV is:
solution:

Two mixers and one TV cost ₹7,000

Two TVs and one mixer cost ₹9,800.

Let the cost of one mixer be M and the cost of one TV be T.

From the given statements, we can write two equations:

2M + T = 7000

2T + M = 9800

From the first equation:

2M + T = 7000

⇒ T = 7000 - 2M

Substitute T = 7000 - 2M in the second equation:

2(7000 - 2M) + M = 9800

⇒ 14000 - 4M + M = 9800

⇒ 14000 - 3M = 9800

⇒ 14000 - 9800 = 3M

⇒ 4200 = 3M

⇒ M = 1400

Substitute M = 1400 back into the equation T = 7000 - 2M:

T = 7000 - 2 × 1400

⇒ T = 7000 - 2800

⇒ T = 4200

**∴ The value of one TV is ₹4,200.**

question: The average age of a group of 32 women is 60 years and that of another group of 40 men is 33 years. The average age of the two groups mixed together is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify ratio of the number of people: Women : Men = 32 : 40 = 4 : 5.

Weighted average = [(Ratio₁ × Avg₁) + (Ratio₂ × Avg₂)] ÷ (Ratio₁ + Ratio₂)

Average age = (4 × 60 + 5 × 33) ÷ (4 + 5)

Average age = (240 + 165) ÷ 9 = 405 ÷ 9 = 45 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of women (n₁) = 32 | Average age (A₁) = 60 years

Number of men (n₂) = 40 | Average age (A₂) = 33 years

**Formula:**

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 
 32 Women: 60 yrs
 
 40 Men: 33 yrs
 
• 
 
 Mixed Average = 45 years
 

 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of women = 32 × 60 = 1920 years

⇒ Total age of men = 40 × 33 = 1320 years

⇒ Total age of combined group = 1920 + 1320 = 3240 years

⇒ Total number of people = 32 + 40 = 72

⇒ Mixed Average = 3240 ÷ 72

⇒ Mixed Average = 45 years

**∴ The correct answer is 45 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

When two groups with different averages are mixed, the resulting average depends on the relative number of elements in each group. Ratio of quantities can be used instead of actual values.

Deviation Method

Assume a temporary average (A). Net Deviation = ∑(nᵢ × (Aᵢ − A)). Correct Average = A + (Net Deviation ÷ Total n).

Alligation Rule

(Quantity 1 ÷ Quantity 2) = (Higher Average − Mixed Average) ÷ (Mixed Average − Lower Average).</p

question: The average age of a class of 39 students is 15 years. If the age of the teacher be included, then the average increases by 3 months. Find the age of the teacher.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Age of Teacher = Initial Average + (New Total Count × Increase in Average)

Initial Average = 15 years

New Total Count (including teacher) = 39 + 1 = 40

Increase = 3 months = 3/12 = 0.25 years

Teacher's Age = 15 + (40 × 0.25) = 15 + 10 = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 39

Average age of students = 15 years

Increase in average = 3 months

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average Age × Number of People

 39 Students Avg = 15 yrs Teacher 
• New Average = 15 years 3 months 
 +3 months Total People = 40 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 39 students = 39 × 15 = 585 years

⇒ New number of people = 39 + 1 = 40

⇒ New average = 15 years + 3 months = 15 years + (3/12) years = 15.25 years

⇒ Total age of 40 people = 40 × 15.25 = 610 years

⇒ Age of Teacher = Total age of 40 people − Total age of 39 students

⇒ Age of Teacher = 610 − 585 = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

When two groups are combined, the new average A = (n₁×A₁ + n₂×A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the number of items and A is the average.

Average of Consecutive Numbers

For any Arithmetic Progression (A.P.), the average is always (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2.

Net Change in Average

If a person of age X is replaced by a person of age Y and the average of 'n' people changes by 'd', then Y = X + (n × d).

question: In a family of six males and a few females, the average monthly consumption of grain per head is 14.4 kg. If the average monthly consumption per head is 20 kg in the case of males and 6 kg in the case of females, find the number of females in the family?
solution:
**Given:**

Number of males in the family = 6

Average monthly consumption of grain per head in the family = 14.4 kg

Average monthly consumption per head for males = 20 kg

Average monthly consumption per head for females = 6 kg

Let's denote the number of females in the family by "f".

**Formula:**

The formula for the average monthly consumption of grain per head in a family with "m" males and "f" females is:

Average monthly consumption per head = (total monthly consumption of grain)/(m + f)

**Calculation:**

Equation 1: Average monthly consumption per head in the family

14.4 = (total monthly consumption of grain)/(6 + f)

Equation 2: Average monthly consumption per head for males and females

20 = (total monthly consumption of grain for males)/6

6 = (total monthly consumption of grain for females)/f

To solve for "f", we can first use Equation 2 to find the total monthly consumption of grain for females:

total monthly consumption of grain for females = 6f

Substitute this into Equation 1 and solve for "f":

14.4 = (total monthly consumption of grain)/(6+f)

14.4 = (total monthly consumption of grain for males + total monthly consumption of grain for females)/(6+f)

14.4 = (20*6 + 6f)/(6+f)

14.4(6+f) = 120 + 6f

86.4 + 14.4f = 120 + 6f

8.4f = 33.6

f = 4

**Therefore, there are 4 females in the family.**

question: The current average age of a family of five members is 24. If the present age of the youngest member in the family is 8 years, what was the average age of the family members just before the birth of this youngest member?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Average age** of **5 members** at the time of **birth** = 24 − 8 = 16 **years**.

**Total sum** of ages of **5 members** 8 years ago = 16 × 5 = 80 **years**.

Just before **birth**, the **family** had only **4 members**.

Required **average age** = 80 ÷ 4 = 20 **years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Current **average age** of **5 members** = 24 **years**.

**Present age** of the **youngest member** = 8 **years**.

**Formula used:**

**Average** = (**Sum of all observations**) ÷ (**Number of observations**)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d9a4ff70b8faafb7459c3cf849321e77e5de7a493e831bcb4fffc0f114ac5f8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total present age** of the **family** = 24 × 5 = 120 **years**.

⇒ **Sum of ages** of the **family** at the time of **birth** = 120 − (5 × 8) **years**.

⇒ **Sum of ages** = 120 − 40 = 80 **years**.

⇒ Just before the **birth**, the number of **members** was 5 − 1 = 4.

⇒ **Average age** then = 80 ÷ 4 = 20 **years**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Sum of Ages

The **total sum** of ages of **'n'** people increases or decreases by **n × t** after **'t'** **years**.

Effect of Birth/Death on Average

When a new person is born, the **number of members** increases, which decreases the **average** if the **total sum** remains constant at that instant.

Uniform Change in Average

If everyone's **age** increases by **'k'** **years**, the **new average** is simply **Old Average + k**.</p

question: The average height of 40 sticks is 156 cm. Some sticks of average height 162 cm are taken out. If the new average height is 150 cm, then how many sticks are remaining?
solution:
Given:

The average height of 40 sticks is 154 cm

Formula used

Average = Sum of all values/Total no. of values

Calculation:

Average of 40 sticks = (Sum of Length of 40 sticks) /40

⇒ 156 = (sum of length 40 sticks) /40

⇒ Sum of length 40 sticks = 6240

Let x sticks be taken out

Average of x sticks = (sum of length of x stick) /x

⇒ 162 = (sum of length of x sticks) /x

⇒ Sum of length of x sticks = 162x

Now, Remaining sticks = 40 - x

Average of (40 - x) sticks = {sum of length of (40 - x) stick} /(40 - x)

⇒ 150 = {sum of length of (40 - x) sticks} /(40 - x)

⇒ Sum of length of (40 - x) sticks = 150(40 - x) = 6000 - 150x

According to the question,

⇒ 162x + 6000 - 150x = 6240

⇒ 12x = 240

⇒ x = 20

Remaining sticks = 40 - x = 40 - 20 = 20

∴ The correct answer is 24.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

Calculation:

Combined average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂)/(n₁ + n₂)

⇒ 156 = [162n + 150(40 - n)]/40

⇒ 6240 = 162n - 150n + 6000

⇒ 12n = 240

⇒ n = 20

Remaining sticks = 40 - n = 40 - 20 = 20

∴ The correct answer is 20.

question: The average weight of some students in class 12th was 56 kg. When seven students whose average weight was 58 kg joined the class, the average weight of all the students increased by 200 gm. Find the number of students in the class in the beginning?
solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of students initially is 56 kg.

Seven students with an average weight of 58 kg joined.

The average weight increased by 200 gm (0.2 kg).

**Concept Used:**

Weighted average and basic algebra.

**Formula Used:**

Total weight of initial students = (number of students) × (average weight)

New average weight = (total weight of all students) / (total number of students)

**Calculation:**

Let the initial number of students be x

⇒ Total initial weight = 56 × x

⇒ Total weight of new students = 58 × 7

⇒ Total weight after new students join = 56 × x + 58 × 7

⇒ New average weight = (56 × x + 58 × 7) / (x + 7)

⇒ New average weight = 56 + 0.2

⇒ (56 × x + 58 × 7) / (x + 7) = 56.2

⇒ 56 × x + 406 = 56.2 × (x + 7)

⇒ 56 × x + 406 = 56.2 × x + 393.4

⇒ 406 - 393.4 = 56.2 × x - 56 × x

⇒ 12.6 = 0.2 × x

⇒ x = 12.6 / 0.2

⇒ x = 63

**∴ The number of students in the class at the beginning was 63.**

question: There are 75 students in the hostel. Due to new admissions, 15 new students join the mess, and the daily expenses of the mess increased by Rs. 240, while the average expenditure per head diminished by Rs. 5. What was the original expenditure (in Rs.) of the mess?
solution:
**Given:**

Initial number of students in the hostel = 75

Number of new students joined = 15

Total students after new admissions = 75 + 15 = 90

Daily expenses of the mess increased by = Rs. 240

Average expenditure per head diminished by = Rs. 5

**Formula Used:**

Original expenditure of the mess = Average expenditure per head × Number of students

**Calculation:**

Let the original average expenditure per head be Rs. x.

⇒ New average expenditure per head = Rs. (x - 5)

Original total expenditure = 75x

New total expenditure = 90 × (x - 5)

It's given that the new total expenditure is Rs. 240 more than the original.

⇒ 90 × (x - 5) = 75x + 240

⇒ 90x - 450 = 75x + 240

⇒ 90x - 75x = 240 + 450

⇒ 15x = 690

⇒ x = 690 / 15

⇒ x = 46

Therefore, original total expenditure = 75 × 46 = Rs. 3450

**The original expenditure of the mess was Rs. 3450.**

question: The average weight of a family of 8 members is 56 kg. The grandfather and the grandmother came to visit the family. Now, the average weight of 10 members of the family is 64 kg. Find the average weight (in kg) of the grandparents.
solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of a family of 8 members = 56 kg

The total number of family members after the grandparents visit = 10

The new average weight of 10 family members = 64 kg

Average weight = Total weight / Number of members

Total weight of the original 8 members = 56 × 8

⇒ Total weight of the original 8 members = 448 kg

Total weight of the 10 members after the grandparents visit = 64 × 10

⇒ Total weight of the 10 members = 640 kg

Weight of the grandparents = Total weight of 10 members - Total weight of 8 members

⇒ Weight of the grandparents = 640 - 448

⇒ Weight of the grandparents = 192 kg

The number of grandparents = 2

Average weight of the grandparents = 192 / 2

⇒ Average weight of the grandparents = 96 kg

**The average weight of the grandparents is 96 kg.**

question: The average weight of Rakesh and his five friends is 62 kg. If Rakesh is 6 kg heavier than the average weight of his five friends, then find the weight of Rakesh.

Average weight of Rakesh and his five friends = 62 kg

Total weight = Average × Number of people

Weight of Rakesh = Average weight of five friends + 6 kg

Weight of Rakesh = x + 6

Total weight of five friends = x × 5

⇒ 372 = 6x + 6

⇒ x = 61

⇒ Weight of Rakesh = 61 + 6

⇒ Weight of Rakesh = 67 kg

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**

question: In an NCC camp, the average weight was 72 kg. If 5 cadets having average weight 76 kg leave and 11 cadets of average weight 79 kg join the group, the average weight of the cadets in the group increases by 0.6 kg. The number of cadets, initially in the group was:
solution:
**Given:**

Initial average weight = 72 kg

Average weight of 5 cadets leaving = 76 kg

Average weight of 11 cadets joining = 79 kg

Increase in average weight = 0.6 kg

**Formula used:**

New total weight = Old total weight - Weight of leaving cadets + Weight of joining cadets

New average = New total weight / New number of cadets

**Calculations:**

Let the initial number of cadets = n

Old total weight = 72 × n

Weight of leaving cadets = 76 × 5 = 380

Weight of joining cadets = 79 × 11 = 869

New total weight = (72 × n) - 380 + 869

New number of cadets = n - 5 + 11 = n + 6

New average = Old average + Increase in average = 72 + 0.6 = 72.6

⇒ dfrac{(72 times n) - 380 + 869}{n + 6} = 72.6

⇒ (72 times n) - 380 + 869 = 72.6 times (n + 6)

⇒ (72 times n) + 489 = 72.6 times n + 435.6

⇒ (72.6 times n) - (72 times n) = 489 - 435.6

⇒ (0.6 times n) = 53.4

⇒ n = dfrac{53.4}{0.6} = 89

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

question: A family of seven minors and some adults has an average wheat consumption of 11.10 kg. The average consumption for minors is 5.5 kg per person, and for adults, it is 16 kg per person. Find the number of adults in the family.
solution:
**Given:**

The family has 7 minors and some adults.

Average wheat consumption of the entire family = 11.10 kg

Average wheat consumption for minors = 5.5 kg per person

Average wheat consumption for adults = 16 kg per person

**Calculation:**

Let the number of adults = x.

Total number of family members = 7 (minors) + x (adults) = 7 + x

Total wheat consumption = (7 × 5.5) + (x × 16)

Average wheat consumption = 11.10

⇒ dfrac{(7 times 5.5) + (x times 16)}{7 + x} = 11.10

⇒ dfrac{38.5 + 16x}{7 + x} = 11.10

⇒ 38.5 + 16x = 11.10 × (7 + x)

⇒ 38.5 + 16x = 77.7 + 11.10x

⇒ 16x - 11.10x = 77.7 - 38.5

⇒ 4.9x = 39.2

⇒ x = dfrac{39.2}{4.9}

⇒ x = 8

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

if A be the term and D be a common difference, then

question: The average of seven consecutive numbers is 95. Find the middle number in the series of seven consecutive numbers.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any arithmetic progression (like consecutive numbers) with an odd number of terms, the average is exactly equal to the middle term.

Total numbers (n) = 7 (which is odd).

Average of the series = 95.

∴ Middle number = Average = 95.

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of consecutive terms = 7

Average of terms = 95

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 x−3 x−2 x−1 x x+1 x+2 x+3 
 Middle Term = Average = 95 7 Consecutive Numbers 

Let the seven consecutive numbers be (x − 3), (x − 2), (x − 1), x, (x + 1), (x + 2), and (x + 3).

⇒ Sum of these 7 numbers = (x − 3) + (x − 2) + (x − 1) + x + (x + 1) + (x + 2) + (x + 3)

⇒ Sum = 7x

⇒ Average = Sum ÷ 7

⇒ 95 = 7x ÷ 7

⇒ x = 95

The middle number in the series is x.

⇒ Middle number = 95.

**∴ The correct answer is 95.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average of Arithmetic Progression (AP)

For any series in AP, the Average = (First Term + Last Term) ÷ 2. In this case, (92 + 98) ÷ 2 = 95.

Middle Term for Even Number of Terms

If there are n terms and n is even, the average is the mean of the two middle terms: [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2.

Consecutive Odd or Even Numbers

For consecutive even or odd numbers, the common difference is 2. The property that the average of an odd number of terms equals the middle term still applies.

Common difference (d) = 2

Using the formula for the nth term of an arithmetic sequence: aₙ = a + (n-1)d

⇒ 71 - 11 = (n-1) × 2

⇒ 60 = (n-1) × 2

⇒ n-1 = 30

⇒ n = 31

Using the formula for the sum of an arithmetic sequence: S_n = (n)/(2) × (a + l)

⇒ S = (31 / 2) × (11 + 71)

⇒ S = (31 / 2) × 82

⇒ S = 31 × 41

⇒ S = 1271

Average:

Average = Sum / Total number of terms

⇒ Average = 1271 / 31

⇒ Average = 41

**The average of all odd numbers from 11 to 71 is 41.**

question: Ravi goes to college from his village at the speed of 5km/h and returns at the speed of 4km/h. If he takes 9 hours in all, find the distance (in km) between the village and the college.
solution:
**Given:**

Speed while going to college = 5 km/h.

Speed while returning = 4 km/h.

Total time taken = 9 hours.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time.

For combined trips with different speeds, use the relationship between distance, speed, and time to set up an equation.

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the village and the college be d kilometers.

Time taken to go to college = d / 5 hours.

Time taken to return = d / 4 hours.

Total time for both trips = Time to go + Time to return = 9 hours.

Setting up the equation:

(d / 5) + (d / 4) = 9

To solve for d, find a common denominator and solve the equation:

(4d + 5d) / 20 = 9

9d = 180

d = 180 / 9

d = 20 kilometers.

**Therefore, the distance between the village and the college is 20 kilometers.**

question: A car travels 80 { km} at 40 { km/h} , 120 { km} at 60 { km/h} , and 100 { km} at 50 { km/h} . Find the average speed.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = 80 + 120 + 100 = 300 km

Total Time = (80/40) + (120/60) + (100/50) = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 hours

Average Speed = 300 ÷ 6 = 50 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ (d₁) = 80 km, Speed₁ (s₁) = 40 km/h

Distance₂ (d₂) = 120 km, Speed₂ (s₂) = 60 km/h

Distance₃ (d₃) = 100 km, Speed₃ (s₃) = 50 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/359f60ac9f91cf196b8615518cd5c15cdd1157190a70637cc619405bddf98a90.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time₁ = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours

⇒ Time₂ = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 hours

⇒ Time₃ = 100 ÷ 50 = 2 hours

⇒ Total Time = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 hours

⇒ Total Distance = 80 + 120 + 100 = 300 km

⇒ Average Speed = 300 ÷ 6 = 50 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 50 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

If a journey is divided into two equal distances traveled at speeds x and y, the average speed is 2xy ÷ (x + y).

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. If they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

question: A car travels 60 km at x km/h, 90 km at y km/h, 120 km at z km/h. If average speed = 60 km/h, x = 30 km/h, y = 45 km/h, find z .
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = 60 + 90 + 120 = 270 km

Total Time = 270 ÷ 60 = 4.5 hours

Time taken for first two parts = (60 ÷ 30) + (90 ÷ 45) = 2 + 2 = 4 hours

Remaining time for z = 4.5 − 4 = 0.5 hours ⇒ z = 120 ÷ 0.5 = 240 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 240 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance₁ (d₁) = 60 km, Speed₁ (x) = 30 km/h

Distance₂ (d₂) = 90 km, Speed₂ (y) = 45 km/h

Distance₃ (d₃) = 120 km, Speed₃ (z) = ?

Average Speed (Vₐvg) = 60 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d768ca7b9f5ff7aa282bb9f9e71cad8439f23fb60f8e62859f8c5d27345ad80f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 60 + 90 + 120 = 270 km

⇒ Total Time (T) = Total Distance ÷ Average Speed

⇒ T = 270 ÷ 60 = 4.5 hours

⇒ Time for 1st segment (t₁) = 60 ÷ 30 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for 2nd segment (t₂) = 90 ÷ 45 = 2 hours

⇒ Time for 3rd segment (t₃) = T − (t₁ + t₂)

⇒ t₃ = 4.5 − (2 + 2) = 4.5 − 4 = 0.5 hours

⇒ Speed z = Distance₃ ÷ t₃

⇒ z = 120 ÷ 0.5 = 240 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 240 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, then Average Speed = 2uv ÷ (u + v).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Relative Speed

If two bodies move at speeds u and v, relative speed is (u + v) in opposite directions and (u − v) in the same direction.

Average weight of Girls = 20 units × 2.5 = 50 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 50 kg.**

Combined meanoverline XA, B = [(number of students in class A × Average weight of student of class A) + (number of students in class B × Average weight of student of class B)]/(Total number of students in class A and B)

**Calculation**

A+ B = 92

A = B + 30% of B

⇒ A = 130B/100

⇒ A = 130 × (92 - A)/100

⇒ A = (11960 - 130A)/100

⇒ 100A = 11960 - 130A

⇒ 230A = 11960

⇒ A = 52

B = 92 - 52

⇒ 40

Let the average weight of students of section A = x

Average weight of students of sectionB = x + 50% of x

⇒150x/100

⇒1.5x

56 = (52 × x + 40 × 1.5x)/92

⇒ 56 × 92 = 52x + 60x

⇒ 5152 = 112x

⇒ x = 5152/112

⇒ x = 46

B = x + 50% of 46

⇒ 46 + 23

⇒ 69

**∴ The average weight (in kg) of students in B is 69.**

question: The average weight of A, B, C and D is 33 kg. C is 12 kg lighter than A, while B is 6 kg heavier than C. D's weight is 10 kg less than that of C. What is the average of A and D?
solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of A, B, C, D = 33 kg

C is 12 kg lighter than A

B is 6 kg heavier than C

D is 10 kg less than that of C

**Concept Used:**

Average = Sum of values ÷ Number of values

**Calculation:**

Let the value of A be x kg.

Weight of C = x – 12 kg

Weight of B = x – 12 + 6 = x – 6 kg

Weight of D = x –12 – 10 = x – 22 kg

So, average of A, B, C and D = (x+x-12+x-6+x-22)/(4)=(4x-40)/(4) = x -10

⇒ x – 10 = 33

⇒ x = 33 + 10 = 43 kg

Then, Weight of A = 43 kg

Weight of D = x –22 = 43 – 22 = 21 kg

Average weight of A and D = (43+21)/(2)=(64)/(2) = 32 kg

**Hence, the average weight of A and D is 32 kg.**

question: In a class of 37 students, there are 22 girls. The average weight of these girls is 46 kg and the average weigh of the whole class is 50 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of the boys in that class? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
solution:
**Given:**

Number of girls = 22

Average weight of girls = 46 kg

Total number of students = 37

Average weight of the whole class = 50 kg

**Formula Used:**

 Average Weight of Boys = (Total Weight of Boys)/(Number of Boys)

 Total Weight of Class = Average Weight of Class times Total Number of Students

 Total Weight of Girls = Average Weight of Girls times Number of Girls

**Calculation:**

Number of boys = Total number of students - Number of girls

⇒ Number of boys = 37 - 22

⇒ Number of boys = 15

⇒ Total weight of the whole class = 50 × 37 = 1850 kg

⇒ Total weight of the girls = 46 × 22 = 1012 kg

⇒ Total weight of the boys = Total weight of the class - Total weight of the girls

⇒ Total weight of the boys = 1850 - 1012 = 838 kg

⇒ Average weight of the boys = 838 / 15 = 55.87 kg

**∴ The average weight of the boys in that class is 55.87 kg.**

question: The average weight of 17 men is 63 kg and the average weight of 36 women is 54 kg. What is the average weight (in kg) of all the men and women together? (Rounded off to the nearest integer)
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the assumed mean (deviation) method to simplify the calculation.

Assume the base average = 54 kg.

Deviation for 17 men = 17 × (63 − 54) = 17 × 9 = +153 kg.

Average deviation per person = +153 ÷ (17 + 36) = 153 ÷ 53 ≈ +2.88 kg.

Combined average = Base average + Average deviation = 54 + 2.88 = 56.88 kg.

Rounding off to the nearest integer gives 57.

**∴ The correct answer is 57 kg.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of men (n₁) = 17, Average weight (A₁) = 63 kg

Number of women (n₂) = 36, Average weight (A₂) = 54 kg

 Weighted Average Visualized as a Balance Scale
 
 
• 
 
 
 36 W
 54 kg
 
 
 17 M
 63 kg
 
 

 Avg ≈ 57 kg
 
 
• 
 
• 
 Ratio: 17 parts
 Ratio: 36 parts

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of men = 17 × 63 = 1071 kg

⇒ Total weight of women = 36 × 54 = 1944 kg

⇒ Total combined weight = 1071 + 1944 = 3015 kg

⇒ Total number of people = 17 + 36 = 53

⇒ Combined average weight = 3015 ÷ 53

⇒ Combined average weight = 56.886... kg

⇒ Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get 57 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 57 kg.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When two or more groups with different quantities are combined, their average is given by Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method

Instead of calculating huge products, assume one value as base average. The true average is Base + (∑ Net Deviations ÷ Total Quantity).

Alligation Rule

Alligation is the reverse visual concept of weighted average. It helps find the ratio in which two groups must be mixed to get a desired average: Ratio = (A₂ − Aw) : (Aw − A₁).

question: The average weight of 20 students of a class was 30.5 kg. After 6 new students joined the class, its average weight increased by 2 kg. Find the average weight of the 6 new students who joined the class (rounded off to one decimal place).
solution:
**Given:**

Average weight of 20 students = 30.5 kg.

After 6 new students joined, average weight increased by 2 kg = 32.5 kg.

**Formula Used:**

Average weight of new students = [New average × (Total number of students after joining) - Old average × (Total number of students before joining)] / Number of new students

**Calculation:**

Total weight of 20 students before joining = 20 × 30.5

Total number of students after 6 joined = 20 + 6 = 26

New average weight after joining = 32.5 kg

Total weight of 26 students after joining = 26 × 32.5

Average weight of 6 new students = [(26 × 32.5) - (20 × 30.5)] / 6

= (845 - 610) / 6

= 235 / 6

= 39.2 kg

**The average weight of the 6 new students who joined the class is 39.2 kg.**

question: The average weight of 20 boys is 60 kg. Together with 30 girls, the average weight of all boys and girls is 54 kg. What is the average weight of 30 girls in kg?
solution:
**Given:**

Number of boys (nb) = 20

Average weight of boys (avgb) = 60 kg

Number of girls (ng) = 30

Average weight of all (avgₐₗₗ) = 54 kg

**Formula Used:**

Sum of weights = Number of individuals × Average weight

**Calculation:**

Total weight of 20 boys = nb × avgb = 20 × 60 = 1200 kg

Total number of boys and girls = nb + ng = 20 + 30 = 50

Total weight of all boys and girls = (nb + ng) × avgₐₗₗ = 50 × 54 = 2700 kg

Total weight of 30 girls = Total weight of all - Total weight of boys

⇒ Total weight of girls = 2700 - 1200 = 1500 kg

Average weight of 30 girls = Total weight of girls / ng

⇒ Average weight of girls = 1500 / 30 = 50 kg

**The average weight of 30 girls is 50 kg.**

question: Five athletes are weighed consecutively, and after each measurement, their average weight is calculated. If the average weight increases by 1.5 kg each time, then how much heavier is the last player than the first player?
solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of the athletes increases by 1.5 kg after each measurement.

There are 5 athletes, and the average weight is calculated after each measurement.

**Formula used:**

Average weight = (Total weight of athletes) / (Number of athletes)

**Calculations:**

Let the weights of the 5 athletes be W1, W2, W3, W4, and W5.

After the first athlete is weighed, the average weight is W1 / 1.

After the second athlete is weighed, the average weight is (W1 + W2) / 2, and it increases by 1.5 kg compared to the previous average.

After the third athlete is weighed, the average weight is (W1 + W2 + W3) / 3, and it again increases by 1.5 kg compared to the previous average.

We know that the average increases by 1.5 kg each time. So, we can write the following equations:

Average after the 2nd athlete = Average after the 1st athlete + 1.5

Average after the 3rd athlete = Average after the 2nd athlete + 1.5

And so on for the 4th and 5th athletes.

Let’s express this in terms of total weights:

For the first athlete: Average = W1 / 1 = W1

For the second athlete: (W1 + W2) / 2 = W1 + 1.5

For the third athlete: (W1 + W2 + W3) / 3 = W1 + 3

For the fourth athlete: (W1 + W2 + W3 + W4) / 4 = W1 + 4.5

For the fifth athlete: (W1 + W2 + W3 + W4 + W5) / 5 = W1 + 6

Now, let’s solve these equations step by step:

From the second equation: (W1 + W2) / 2 = W1 + 1.5

W1 + W2 = 2(W1 + 1.5) = 2W1 + 3

W2 = 2W1 + 3 - W1 = W1 + 3

From the third equation: (W1 + W2 + W3) / 3 = W1 + 3

W1 + W2 + W3 = 3(W1 + 3) = 3W1 + 9

W1 + (W1 + 3) + W3 = 3W1 + 9

2W1 + 3 + W3 = 3W1 + 9

W3 = 3W1 + 9 - 2W1 - 3 = W1 + 6

From the fourth equation: (W1 + W2 + W3 + W4) / 4 = W1 + 4.5

W1 + W2 + W3 + W4 = 4(W1 + 4.5) = 4W1 + 18

W1 + (W1 + 3) + (W1 + 6) + W4 = 4W1 + 18

3W1 + 9 + W4 = 4W1 + 18

W4 = 4W1 + 18 - 3W1 - 9 = W1 + 9

From the fifth equation: (W1 + W2 + W3 + W4 + W5) / 5 = W1 + 6

W1 + W2 + W3 + W4 + W5 = 5(W1 + 6) = 5W1 + 30

W1 + (W1 + 3) + (W1 + 6) + (W1 + 9) + W5 = 5W1 + 30

4W1 + 18 + W5 = 5W1 + 30

W5 = 5W1 + 30 - 4W1 - 18 = W1 + 12

Now, to find how much heavier the last player (W5) is compared to the first player (W1):

W5 - W1 = (W1 + 12) - W1 = 12

**Therefore, the last player is 12 kg heavier than the first player.**

question: In a group of 200 members, 45% are teenagers and the remaining are adults. The average weight of the whole group is 62 kg. If the average weight of teenagers is 56 kg, then the nearest integral value of the average weight of adults is ______.

**∴ Average weight of adults = 67 kg**

question: Out of four numbers, the average of the first three is 16 and that of the last three is 15. If the last number is 21 then the first number is:
solution:
**Concept:**

Average = Sum of observation / Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

The last 3 numbers total = 3 × 15 = 45

So the middle 2 numbers will add to 45 – 21 = 24

First 3 numbers total = 3 × 16 = 48

So the first number is 48 – 24 = 24

∴ The first number is 24

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

There are four numbers A, B, C and D

Average of first 3 numbers = 16

Sum of first 3 numbers = 16 × 3 = 48

⇒ A + B + C = 48 --- (1)

Average of last 3 numbers = 15

Sum of last 3 numbers = 3 × 15 = 45

⇒ B + C + D = 45 --- (2)

Subtract equation (2) from equation (1)

⇒ A – D = 48 – 45

⇒ A – D = 3

⇒ A – 21 = 3 (∵ D = 21)

⇒ A = 3 + 21 = 24

**∴ The first number is 24**

subject: MATH
question: The sum of five numbers A, B, C, D and E is 37.5. The average of A and B is 6, and the average of D and E is 9. The average of A, B and C is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **sum of all five numbers** A, B, C, D, and E is given as 37.5.

The **sum of D and E** is 2 × 9 = 18.

Subtract the sum of D and E from the total sum to find the **sum of A, B, and C**: 37.5 − 18 = 19.5.

The **average of A, B, and C** is the sum divided by 3: 19.5 ÷ 3 = 6.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of five numbers (A + B + C + D + E) = 37.5

Average of A and B = 6

Average of D and E = 9

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Average = Sum ÷ Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d61f9deff71744e67dd683b3cdab22a0b6566cab0c5d898c55c387c456b5feb3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of A and B = 2 × 6 = 12

⇒ Sum of D and E = 2 × 9 = 18

⇒ Substitute these in the total sum equation: (A + B) + C + (D + E) = 37.5

⇒ 12 + C + 18 = 37.5

⇒ 30 + C = 37.5

⇒ C = 37.5 − 30 = 7.5

⇒ Sum of A, B, and C = (A + B) + C = 12 + 7.5 = 19.5

⇒ Average of A, B, and C = 19.5 ÷ 3 = 6.5

**∴ The correct answer is 6.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

The average of n numbers is calculated as (Sum of all n numbers) ÷ n.

Relationship between Sum and Average

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations. This is used to find individual components when the total is known.

Weighted Average

When combining groups, the combined average is (n₁ × Avg₁ + n₂ × Avg₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

question: There are 100 students in a class, out of which 70% are girls and others are boys. The average score of girls in a test is 20% more than that of boys. If the average score of all the students is 57, then what is the average score of boys?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Girls** to **Boys** = 70 : 30 = 7 : 3.

Ratio of their average scores = 120% : 100% = 6 : 5.

Weighted average units = (7 × 6 + 3 × 5) ÷ (7 + 3) = (42 + 15) ÷ 10 = 5.7 units.

Given 5.7 units = 57 ⇒ 1 unit = 10.

Average score of boys = 5 units = 5 × 10 = 50.

**∴ The correct answer is 50.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total students = 100, **Girls** = 70%, **Boys** = 30%, Total Average = 57.

**Formula Used:** Total Score = Number of Students × Average Score

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c884f44a904f4f2ab128e6f1409623d5719bb27c779e7baab3d187fd3c1f0460.png] 

⇒ Total **Girls** = 70 and Total **Boys** = 30

⇒ Let the **Average score of boys** = x

⇒ **Average score of girls** = x + 20% of x = 1.2x

⇒ Total class score = (70 × 1.2x) + (30 × x)

⇒ 100 × 57 = 84x + 30x

⇒ 5700 = 114x

⇒ x = 5700 ÷ 114

⇒ x = 50

**∴ The correct answer is 50.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Formula

The combined average of two groups is calculated as (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and a is the average.

Percentage Increase

If a value increases by r%, the new value is Base × (100 + r) ÷ 100. Here, 20% more means a multiplier of 1.2.

Mixture and Alligation

The ratio of quantities is inversely proportional to the deviations of their individual averages from the mean average.</p

Let the numbers be a, b, and c

According to the question

⇒ {a + bover 2} + c = 154

⇒ a + b + 2c = 308

⇒ 2c = 308 - a - b ----(1)

⇒ {b + cover 2} + a = 148

⇒ b + c + 2a = 296

2a = 296 - b - c ----(2)

⇒ {c + aover 2} + b = 132

⇒ c + a + 2b = 264

⇒ 2b = 264 - a - c ----(3)

By adding all equation

⇒ 2a + 2b + 2c = 308 - a - b + 296 - b - c + 264 - a - c

⇒ 2a + 2b + 2c = 868 - 2a - 2b - 2c

⇒ a + b + c = {868over 4}

⇒ a + b + c = 217 ----(4)

By solving equation (4) and (1)

⇒ 217 - c + 2c = 308

⇒ c = 308 - 217

⇒ c = 91

By equation (2) and (4)

⇒ 217 - a + 2a = 296

⇒ a = 296 - 217

⇒ a = 79

By equation (3) and (4)

⇒ 217 - b + 2b = 264

⇒ b = 264 - 217 = 47

The average of all three numbers = {91 + 79 + 47over 3} = {217over 3} = {72{1over 3}}

**∴ The required result will be {72{1over 3}}.**

question: The average of 30 numbers is 36. If Z is subtracted from each of these 30 numbers, then the average becomes 28. What is the value of Z?
solution:
**Given:**

The average of 30 numbers is 36.

If Z is subtracted from each of these 30 numbers, then the average becomes 28.

**To find:**

The value of Z.

**Formula used:**

We can use the formula:

New sum = Old sum - nZ

Where,

The new sum is the sum of the new set of numbers obtained by subtracting Z from each of the original numbers.

The old sum is the sum of the original set of numbers.

n is the number of terms in the set.

**Solution:**

Let us assume that the sum of the 30 numbers is S.

According to the given information,

The average of the 30 numbers is 36. Therefore, the sum of the 30 numbers is 30 × 36 = 1080.

If Z is subtracted from each of these 30 numbers, then the average becomes 28. Therefore, the sum of the new set of numbers is 30 × 28 = 840.

Using the formula, we get:

New sum = Old sum - nZ

⇒ 840 = 1080 - 30Z

⇒ 30Z = 240

⇒ Z = 8

**Therefore, the value of Z is 8.**

question: What is the average of 12.5, 18.4, 15.5, 16.6, and 20.4?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **Assumed Mean** of 16.

Calculate **deviations** from 16: −3.5, +2.4, −0.5, +0.6, and +4.4.

Net deviation = (−3.5 − 0.5) + (2.4 + 0.6 + 4.4) = −4.0 + 7.4 = +3.4.

Average correction = Net deviation ÷ Total terms = 3.4 ÷ 5 = 0.68.

Actual Average = Assumed Mean + Correction = 16 + 0.68 = 16.68.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.68.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 12.5, 18.4, 15.5, 16.6, and 20.4.

**Formula Used:** Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb099920044e9d60cae89c86981fd15b63071bdfee0786b20ed7b2dcbae92785.png] 

⇒ Sum = 12.5 + 18.4 + 15.5 + 16.6 + 20.4

⇒ Sum = 83.4

⇒ Number of terms = 5

⇒ Average = 83.4 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 16.68

**∴ The correct answer is 16.68.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The **mean** (average) is the central value of a set of numbers, calculated as Sum ÷ Count.

Properties of Average

If each observation is increased or decreased by a **constant k**, the new average also increases or decreases by **k**.

Weighted Average

When sets have different sizes n₁ and n₂ with averages x₁ and x₂, the **combined average** is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

question: The average of numbers A and B is 16. The average of numbers B and C is 40. What is the difference between C and A?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in averages of (B, C) and (A, B) = 40 − 16 = 24.

Since both sets consist of 2 numbers and B is common, the difference between the unique numbers is double the difference of their averages.

Difference between C and A = 2 × 24 = 48.

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of A and B = 16

Average of B and C = 40

**Formula Used:**

Sum of numbers = Average × Number of items

 
 A + B = 32
 
 B + C = 80
 
• 
 
• 
 

 Difference (C − A) = 80 − 32 = 48
 Sum Comparison

**Calculations:**

⇒ Average of A and B = (A + B) ÷ 2 = 16

⇒ A + B = 16 × 2 = 32 → (Eq. 1)

⇒ Average of B and C = (B + C) ÷ 2 = 40

⇒ B + C = 40 × 2 = 80 → (Eq. 2)

Subtracting (Eq. 1) from (Eq. 2):

⇒ (B + C) − (A + B) = 80 − 32

⇒ B + C − A − B = 48

⇒ C − A = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Difference Property

If Average(x, y) = M and Average(y, z) = N, then the difference (z − x) = 2 × (N − M).

Weighted Average

Weighted Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the quantity and x is the value/average.</p

⇒ Time taken = Distance/Speed = 480/(x + 10)

⇒ (480/x) - 4 = 480/(x + 10)

⇒ (480- 4x)/x = 480/(x + 10)

⇒ (480 - 4x)(x + 10) = 480x

⇒ 480x + 4800 - 4x² - 40x = 480x

 

⇒ 4x² + 40x - 4800 = 0 

⇒ x² + 10x - 1200 = 0 

⇒ x2 + 40x - 30x - 1200 = 0

⇒ x(x + 40) - 30(x + 40) = 0

⇒ (x + 40)(x - 30) = 0

⇒ x = -40, 30 

∵ Speed cannot be negative 

**∴ The required answer is __30__. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Distance = (X × Y)/(X - Y) [time difference]

⇒ [x × (x + 10)/10] × 4 = 480

⇒ x(x + 10) = 1200

⇒ x × (x + 10) = 30 × 40

⇒ x = 30 km/hr

question: Average of 8 numbers is 44. The average of first three numbers is 50 and the average of next two numbers is 52. If the sixth number is 6 and 8 less than seventh and eighth number respectively, then what is the value of eighth number?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of 8 numbers = 8 × 44 = 352.

Sum of first five numbers = (3 × 50) + (2 × 52) = 150 + 104 = 254.

Sum of last three numbers (6th, 7th, and 8th) = 352 − 254 = 98.

As 6th is 6 and 8 less than 7th and 8th: 3 × (6th number) + 6 + 8 = 98.

6th number = (98 − 14) ÷ 3 = 28.

8th number = 28 + 8 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 8 numbers = 44

Average of first 3 numbers = 50

Average of next 2 numbers = 52

6th number = 7th number − 6 = 8th number − 8

**Formula Used:**

Sum = Average × Number of terms

 
 
• 
 
• 
 First 3 (Avg: 50)
 Next 2 (Avg: 52)
 Last 3 (Sum: 98)
 Total Average = 44 (Sum = 352)
 

 6th: x
 7th: x+6
 8th: x+8

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of all 8 numbers = 8 × 44 = 352

⇒ Sum of first 3 numbers = 3 × 50 = 150

⇒ Sum of next 2 numbers = 2 × 52 = 104

⇒ Sum of 6th, 7th, and 8th numbers = 352 − (150 + 104) = 98

⇒ Let the 6th number be x.

⇒ 7th number = x + 6

⇒ 8th number = x + 8

⇒ x + (x + 6) + (x + 8) = 98

⇒ 3x + 14 = 98

⇒ 3x = 98 − 14 = 84

⇒ x = 28

⇒ 8th number = 28 + 8 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Weighted Average

When groups have different averages: Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂ + ...) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ...).

Sum of Deviations

The algebraic sum of deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero.</p

question: The average of 10 numbers is 8. If each number is multiplied by 10, then the new average will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If every observation in a dataset is multiplied by a constant k, the new average is simply the old average multiplied by k.

Old average = 8

Constant multiplier = 10

New average = 8 × 10 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 10 numbers = 8

Multiplier for each number = 10

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all numbers ÷ Total count of numbers

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5300089b3b3c887596bd66d0fc303b520d088857f3a2f05ef83c5dfc3dc8b428.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the 10 numbers be x₁, x₂, ..., x₁₀

⇒ Sum of the original numbers = x₁ + x₂ + ... + x₁₀ = 8 × 10 = 80

⇒ When each number is multiplied by 10, the new numbers are 10x₁, 10x₂, ..., 10x₁₀

⇒ Sum of the new numbers = 10x₁ + 10x₂ + ... + 10x₁₀

⇒ Sum of the new numbers = 10 × (x₁ + x₂ + ... + x₁₀)

⇒ Sum of the new numbers = 10 × 80 = 800

⇒ New average = Sum of the new numbers ÷ 10

⇒ New average = 800 ÷ 10 = 80

**∴ The correct answer is 80.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition & Subtraction Property of Averages

If a constant value 'c' is added to or subtracted from every number in a dataset, the new average becomes (Original Average ± c).

Multiplication & Division Property of Averages

If every number in a dataset is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant 'k', the new average becomes (Original Average × k) or (Original Average ÷ k).

Combined Average

For two separate groups with sizes n₁ and n₂ and individual averages A₁ and A₂, the Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
</p

Deviation of 15 students from average = 180 − 170 = +10 cm.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of the two numbers = 48 × 2 = 96.

New sum after adding 3 to the smaller number = 96 + 3 = 99.

Ratio of (Smaller + 3) : (Larger) = 11 : 20.

Total ratio parts = 11 + 20 = 31 units.

Larger number = (20 ÷ 31) × 99 = 1980 ÷ 31 ≈ 63.87.

**∴ The correct answer is 63.87.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

question: If the average of two numbers is 12 and the product of the same two numbers is 119, then the difference of those two numbers is:
solution:
**Given:**

Average of two numbers = 12.

Product of the same two numbers = 119.

**Formula Used:**

Let the two numbers be x and y.

Average = (x + y) / 2

Product = x × y

**Calculation:**

Given, Average = 12 ⇒ (x + y) / 2 = 12

⇒ x + y = 24 ⇒ (1)

Given, Product = 119 ⇒ x × y = 119 ⇒ (2)

From equation (1), y = 24 - x

Substitute y in equation (2),

x × (24 - x) = 119

⇒ 24x - x² = 119

⇒ x² - 24x + 119 = 0

Solving the quadratic equation,

x² - 17x - 7x + 119 = 0

x(x - 17) - 7(x - 17) = 0

(x - 17)(x - 7) = 0

⇒ x = 17 or x = 7

If x = 17, then y = 7 (from y = 24 - x)

If x = 7, then y = 17 (from y = 24 - x)

Therefore, the difference of those two numbers = |x - y| = |17 - 7| = 10

**The difference of those two numbers is 10.**

question: If the average of 7, x, 13, 16 and 9 is 10, then the value of x is:

__Shortcut Trick__

Net deviation from the average (10) must be zero.

Deviations of known numbers: (7−10) + (13−10) + (16−10) + (9−10)

⇒ −3 + 3 + 6 − 1 = +5

To balance +5, x must have a deviation of −5 from the average.

x = 10 − 5 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Numbers: 7, x, 13, 16, 9

Total Count (n): 5

Average: 10

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

⇒ (7 + x + 13 + 16 + 9) ÷ 5 = 10

⇒ (45 + x) ÷ 5 = 10

⇒ 45 + x = 10 × 5

⇒ 45 + x = 50

⇒ x = 50 − 45

⇒ x = 5

question: The average expenditure of 32 persons is ₹6,000 and that of another 40 persons is ₹3,300. The average expenditure of the whole group is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of persons = 32 : 40 = **4 : 5**

Let the assumed average be **₹3,300**. Deviation in first group = 6,000 − 3,300 = **2,700**

Total extra = 4 × 2,700 = 10,800. Divide this by total ratio parts (4 + 5 = 9).

Average increase = 10,800 ÷ 9 = **1,200**

Actual Average = 3,300 + 1,200 = **₹4,500**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of persons in Group 1 (n₁) = **32**

Average expenditure of Group 1 (A₁) = **₹6,000**

Number of persons in Group 2 (n₂) = **40**

Average expenditure of Group 2 (A₂) = **₹3,300**

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/76706bc47fe61fd0ca6d3c0e7fc3f18359493cb15584193d4efd6c11aa43eb09.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total expenditure of 32 persons = 32 × 6,000 = **₹1,92,000**

⇒ Total expenditure of 40 persons = 40 × 3,300 = **₹1,32,000**

⇒ Total expenditure of the whole group = 1,92,000 + 1,32,000 = **₹3,24,000**

⇒ Total number of persons = 32 + 40 = **72**

⇒ Average expenditure of whole group = 3,24,000 ÷ 72

⇒ Average expenditure = **₹4,500**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

question: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 80, and that of the rest is 70. What is the average score of the whole class?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume the base **average score** is 70.

Deviation for the first 12 students = 12 × (80 − 70) = +120.

Distributed deviation for all **30 students** = 120 ÷ 30 = 4.

Total average score = Base average + Deviation = 70 + 4 = 74.

**∴ The correct answer is 74.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of **students** = 30

Number of students in the first group = 12

**Average score** of the first group = 80

Number of students in the second group = 30 − 12 = 18

**Average score** of the second group = 70

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = Total Sum of Scores ÷ Total Number of Students

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3af5b3b6f69080c8dc76d0535b3d7da80c0ce202cfb3de8b66865729a96d1e43.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total score of 12 students = 12 × 80 = 960

⇒ Total score of the remaining 18 students = 18 × 70 = 1260

⇒ Total score of the whole class = 960 + 1260 = 2220

⇒ Average score of 30 students = 2220 ÷ 30

⇒ Average score = 74

**∴ The correct answer is 74.**

**__Additional Information__**

Combined Mean Formula

The combined mean (x꜀) of two groups is calculated as: x꜀ = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the size and x is the average of each group.

Weighted Average

Used when items in a data set have different levels of importance or frequency; each value is multiplied by its weight before summing and dividing by the total weight.

Deviation Method

A mental math technique where an assumed mean is used, and the net deviation from this mean is adjusted across the total count to find the actual average.</p

question: The average of a non-zero number and its square is 7 times the number. The number is:
solution:
**Given:**

The average of a non-zero number and its square is 7 times the number.

Calculation:

Average = (number + square of the number) ÷ 2

Average = 7 × number

Let the number be x.

(x + x²) ÷ 2 = 7x

⇒ x + x² = 14x

⇒ x² + x - 14x = 0

⇒ x² - 13x = 0

⇒ x(x - 13) = 0

⇒ x = 0 or x = 13

Since the number is non-zero, x = 13.

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

question: The average of two numbers is 13.5 and the square root of their product is 6sqrt{5}. Find the numbers.
solution:
**Given:**

Average of two numbers = 13.5

Average = (a + b) / 2

Quadratic equation: x² - (a + b)x + (a × b) = 0

**Calculations:**

Factor pairs of 180 summing to 27: 12 and 15

⇒ (x - 12)(x - 15) = 0

subject: MATH
question: Two classes took the same test. One class of 20 students made an average grade of 85%, the other class of 30 students made an average grade of 70%. The average grade for all students across both classes is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of students in **Class 1** and **Class 2** = 20 : 30 = 2 : 3.

Using the **Deviation Method**: Let the assumed average be 70%.

Deviation for Class 1 = (85% − 70%) = +15% per student.

Net deviation for 2 units = 2 × 15% = +30%.

Distribute net deviation over total ratio parts (2 + 3 = 5): 30% ÷ 5 = 6%.

Final average = Assumed average + deviation = 70% + 6% = 76%.

**∴ The correct answer is 76%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students in **Class A** (n₁) = 20 | Average grade (A₁) = 85%

Number of students in **Class B** (n₂) = 30 | Average grade (A₂) = 70%

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = [(n₁ × A₁) + (n₂ × A₂)] ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ad3855b7f409d1957821bfcdcdd6c7abc81be49fd97d344d3c0b6245c5ed2669.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of grades for Class A = 20 × 85 = 1700

⇒ Total sum of grades for Class B = 30 × 70 = 2100

⇒ Total sum of grades for both classes = 1700 + 2100 = 3800

⇒ Total number of students = 20 + 30 = 50

⇒ **Average grade** for all students = 3800 ÷ 50

⇒ Combined Average = 76%

**∴ The correct answer is 76%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Principle

When two groups with different averages are combined, the **resultant average** lies closer to the average of the larger group (in this case, 70% because Class 2 has 30 students).

Ratio and Alligation

The difference between the averages and the mean is **inversely proportional** to the number of students: (85 − 76) : (76 − 70) = 9 : 6 = 3 : 2, which matches the student ratio 30 : 20.

General Formula for n Groups

Weighted Average = (∑nᵢAᵢ) ÷ ∑nᵢ, where n is the number of items and A is the value of each item.</p

question: A man's average driving speed for 9 hours is 88 km/hr. During the first five hours of his journey, he drove at 74 km/hr, and last two hours he drove at 82 km/hr. What was his average speed (in km/hr) for the sixth and the seventh hour?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Overall **average speed** for 9 hr = 88 km/hr.

Net deviation for first 5 hr = 5 × (74 − 88) = −70 km.

Net deviation for last 2 hr = 2 × (82 − 88) = −12 km.

Total deficit = −70 − 12 = −82 km.

The 6th and 7th hr must compensate for this deficit: 88 + (82 ÷ 2) = 129 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 129 km/hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total **time** = 9 hr, Total **average speed** = 88 km/hr.

**Time segment 1** = 5 hr, **Speed** = 74 km/hr.

**Time segment 3** = 2 hr, **Speed** = 82 km/hr.

**Formula:** **Total Distance** = **Average Speed** × **Total Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b0cd4d6d7565920a775a3604fd52ed2104d25f0fdd8800b007b550ff61be3f1c.png] 

⇒ **Total Distance** = 88 × 9 = 792 km

⇒ **Distance** in first 5 hr = 74 × 5 = 370 km

⇒ **Distance** in last 2 hr = 82 × 2 = 164 km

⇒ **Sum** of known distances = 370 + 164 = 534 km

⇒ **Remaining distance** (6th + 7th hr) = 792 − 534 = 258 km

⇒ **Average speed** for 6th and 7th hr = 258 ÷ 2 = 129 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 129 km/hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

When time intervals are equal, the **Average Speed** is the **Arithmetic Mean** of the individual speeds: Vₐvg = (v₁ + v₂ + ... + vₙ) ÷ n.

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds 'a' and 'b', the **Average Speed** is the **Harmonic Mean**: 2ab ÷ (a + b).

Weighted Average Method

The overall average speed can be calculated using the **weighted average** formula: Vₐvg = (n₁v₁ + n₂v₂ + ...) ÷ (n₁ + n₂ + ...), where n represents the time spent at each speed.</p

question: The average of five numbers is 206. The average of two of them is 205. The average of another two of those numbers is 207.5. How many numbers can be accurately identified with this information?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Sum** of 5 numbers = 206 × 5 = 1030

**Sum of 4 numbers** = (205 × 2) + (207.5 × 2) = 410 + 415 = 825

**Fifth number** = 1030 − 825 = 205

The other numbers only have fixed **sums**, not fixed individual values.

**∴ The correct answer is One.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 5 numbers = 206 | Average of pair 1 = 205 | Average of pair 2 = 207.5

**Formula Used:** Sum = Average × Number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5d0b80dd23066d26bfd7ea4c5252e046bec61eb1f48dcfc422ac9fb35d78d627.png] 

⇒ **Total Sum** of 5 numbers = 206 × 5 = 1030

⇒ **Sum** of first two numbers = 205 × 2 = 410

⇒ **Sum** of another two numbers = 207.5 × 2 = 415

⇒ Let the numbers be a, b, c, d, and e.

⇒ (a + b) + (c + d) + e = 1030

⇒ 410 + 415 + e = 1030

⇒ 825 + e = 1030

⇒ e = 1030 − 825 = 205

⇒ While **e** is fixed at 205, the pairs (a, b) and (c, d) can have infinite combinations that satisfy their respective sums.

**∴ The correct answer is One.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

The average or mean is calculated as the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations (Mean = Σx ÷ n).

Sum of Observations

If the average of **n** numbers is **A**, then their total sum is always **n × A**.

Identifiability in Averages

To identify individual values from a group average, you need **n − 1** independent equations or constraints for a group of **n** items.</p

question: In a class, there are 30 boys and 20 girls. The average score of boys in Physics is 92, whereas the average score of girls in Physics is 83. Find the average score of the whole class in Physics.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = 30 : 20 = 3 : 2

Assume a base average of 83. Deviation for boys = 92 − 83 = +9

Total deviation = 3 × 9 = 27

Net increase in average = 27 ÷ (3 + 2) = 27 ÷ 5 = 5.4

Final Average = 83 + 5.4 = 88.4

**∴ The correct answer is 88.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **boys** (n₁) = 30, Average score (A₁) = 92

Number of **girls** (n₂) = 20, Average score (A₂) = 83

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35f4ec81271da01979351256869a2ada87b899cf99f143e53bb9722e3f511f70.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks of **boys** = 30 × 92 = 2760

⇒ Total marks of **girls** = 20 × 83 = 1660

⇒ Total marks of the **whole class** = 2760 + 1660 = 4420

⇒ Total number of students = 30 + 20 = 50

⇒ Average score of the class = 4420 ÷ 50

⇒ Average score of the class = 88.4

**∴ The correct answer is 88.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

When two groups with different averages are combined, the resulting average is closer to the group with the **larger number of members**.

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For a set of numbers in **A.P.**, the average is simply the arithmetic mean of the first and last term: (First + Last) ÷ 2.

Effect of Constant Values

If each value in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the new average also increases or decreases by **k**.</p

question: In a mock test conducted by a coaching institute, 20 students average scored 75% marks and the remaining 15 students average scored 54% marks. Find the average score.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of students = 20 : 15 = 4 : 3

Difference in average = 75% − 54% = 21%

Net surplus to distribute = 4 × 21% = 84%

Distributed surplus = 84% ÷ (4 + 3) = 12%

Average score = 54% + 12% = 66%

**∴ The correct option is A.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students in Group 1 (n₁) = 20

Average score of Group 1 (A₁) = 75%

Number of students in Group 2 (n₂) = 15

Average score of Group 2 (A₂) = 54%

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 
 20 Students
